text:
I had an ideal—where is it?

I harbored a virtue—why has it gone?

I was a Templar—where is my sturdy mail?

On what bloodied field of battle

did they leave me, sad and defeated?


O Progress, you are light! Why does your radiance

not fill my conscience? I am afraid

of the terrible doubt that poisons,

and you watch me roll upon the sand

and, like a grim vestal, lower your finger!


O decadent century, you who boast

of possessing truth, you who pride yourself

on making pacts with God and death,

give me back my faith; I am a Chactas

caressing the corpse of his Atala...


I loved, and you told me: “Analyze,”

and my passion died; I fought fiercely,

with Jesus as armor, piece by piece,

against the penetrating edge of your steel.


I thirst to know and you do not teach me;

I thirst to advance and you do not help me;

I thirst to believe and you hurl me

into the sea of theories where you dream

of finding solutions to your doubts!


And I fall, you see, and can no longer

fight without love, without serene faith

to light my path, and I am afraid...

Receive me, for God’s sake! Raise your finger,

vestal, lest they kill me in the arena!

translation.title: Incoherences
translation.editorial_note: The translation retains the poem’s formal address to Progress and its allusions to Chactas, Atala, and the Templar, preserving the paradox of knowledge as both light and abandonment.
